clue.text: Piano used in his art? Wrong!

definitions.text: Piano used in his art? Wrong!

indicators.note: the piano letter is put to use inside the other letters, so it goes into them
the words his art are set wrong, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a musician for bringing a piano into their performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' turns HIS ART into HARIST, and 'used in' puts P inside it. As a whole the clue is also the definition: a harp player's art indeed has no piano in it, so the idea is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp player's craft is plucked strings, so bringing a keyboard into it would be a mistake.

clue.text: Boatman associated with the Tweed

definitions.meaning: One of the three oarsmen in Jerome K Jerome's Three Men in a Boat
... Tweed is the hand-woven cloth from the Outer Hebrides

explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed suggests the river on the Scottish border, but the second sense is the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a comic rower in a Victorian novel and to a famous woollen fabric.

clue.text: New guard set up, having pulled out another lot?

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a warder is a prison guard

explanation.surface: A fresh sentry is installed after drawing a second ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns N + WARDER, in this down clue, into the answer. The definition is playful: drawing lots again.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw again is to pull out another ticket or lot, as in a repeated raffle.

clue.text: Lodging-house proprietor shot outside tower

indicators.note: outside means the shot's word goes round the tower's

parts.note: an inner is a shot in archery or shooting hitting the ring next to the bull
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A boarding-house owner is gunned down outside a castle tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a verb about the proprietor shot dead, but it names a hit in archery just outside the bull, and 'outside' wraps it round the castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs an inn, a house giving travellers lodging.

clue.text: Passed over male for broadcast

indicators.note: over says the first word's letters lie over and around the abbreviation for male

parts.note: to transit is to pass across; transitted is a doubled-t spelling of its past tense

explanation.surface: A man was overlooked for a radio slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' reads as overlooked, but 'Passed' is TRANSITTED and 'over' puts M inside it. The doubled T is a less usual spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that has been transmitted has gone out over the air.

clue.text: Weak young, creature brought back by detectives

indicators.note: the young creature's word is brought back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: a calf is a young cow, a young creature
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A feeble baby animal is returned home by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the baby animal to make FLAC; British crosswords use CID for detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaccid means limp and lacking firmness, hence feeble.

clue.text: Section of poem meeting required standard

definitions.meaning: an old word for a canto or part of a poem or song
suitable or up to the mark

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a canto shares its spelling with the adjective for suitable.

clue.text: Tree originally seen in an enclosure

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: an gives the article A
a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A tree first noticed inside a paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S, and 'in' puts it inside A + PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Height I have raised in shelter for sheep

indicators.note: in places the height and raised contraction inside the shelter word

parts.note: a cot is a small shelter for animals, as in sheepcote

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the contraction is read upwards

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A hill is built up to protect the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the contraction upwards to EVI, and 'in' puts it with the height letter inside the shelter. 'shelter for sheep' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviot is a hardy white-faced sheep breed named after hills on the English-Scottish border.

clue.text: Calamity associated with Kipling's triumph

definitions.meaning: Kipling's poem If speaks of meeting with Triumph and its twin impostor, the two named together

explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is the second impostor paired with triumph in Kipling's poem.

clue.text: Superfluous leftist and German worker

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, a leftist
und is the German word for and
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A left-wing German labourer is surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and German' asks for the word and in German, UND, not for the conjunction plus a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is no longer needed, more than is wanted.

clue.text: Publishers make an insistent demand

definitions.meaning: the newspaper and publishing world collectively

explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper trade is called after the printing machine, and to urge hard is to push.

clue.text: Only June ends up in this silly fashion

definitions.meaning: of the twelve months only June has the letter E as its last letter, so it alone finishes in that vowel

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that June alone ends in a ridiculous way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is whimsical: among month names only June finishes up 'in an E', which, run together, spells the answer. 'in this ... fashion' just links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, the same as silly.

clue.text: Scan Times letters for meaningful analysis

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken and rearranged to stand for something else

explanation.surface: Reading a newspaper's letters page closely in search of real meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times letters' looks like the newspaper's correspondence page, but it means the letters of SCAN TIMES, which 'letters for' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the study of meaning in language, an analysis of what words signify.

clue.text: Arab in state festivity reveals delusions of grandeur

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: in puts the Arab inside the festivity

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
an Omani is a native of Oman, an Arab state

explanation.surface: An Arab at a national celebration shows a grand idea of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' could be any country, but here it is a US state by its postal code; 'in' puts the Arab inside the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Megalomania is an obsessive belief in one's own power and importance.

clue.text: Cold-blooded sort of photographer?

parts.note: a cold-blooded creature is a reptile, and a photographer who takes quick shots is snapping; the reptile here is a fierce freshwater one that bites

explanation.definitionFit: This North American reptile is cold-blooded and known for its biting jaws, its snap.

clue.text: Turned out novel, though lacking schooling

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of turned out take a new form

explanation.surface: An author produced a book despite never having been taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the signal to rearrange TURNED OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untutored has had no teaching or formal education.

clue.text: Steel container

parts.note: steel here is poetic for a blade or sword, so the container is what holds a sword

explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath for a sword, the cold steel of old poetry.

clue.text: Bravos are making court angry a lot, possibly

definitions.note: the definition is a predicate: shouts of bravo are full of praise

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of court angry a lot could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Cheering in a law court is making the judges very cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges COURT ANGRY A LOT; 'making' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of bravo express praise and good wishes for someone's success.

clue.text: Most orderly home to dine in

indicators.note: in puts the dining word inside the home word

parts.note: a nest is a home
to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: The tidiest house in which to have dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the dining word inside the home word; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: Magistrate again punishing oil company employee?

definitions.meaning: a magistrate who fines someone a second time would be a re-fine-r, a fining one again
someone who works at a refinery purifying crude oil

explanation.surface: A judge fines a petrol worker a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is purified at a plant where such a worker is employed.

clue.text: A way eastern sailors assembled at rear

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
E is the abbreviation for eastern; the answer also sits inside this word, but that is a coincidence the setter does not use
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors gathered at the back of the ship heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' only links the four pieces, which stand side by side; RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for behind or at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Minor official position in sight? Then sit back

parts.note: the bead is the small knob on a gun barrel, seen in the sight when aiming

indicators.note: back says the word for sitting is read backwards

parts.note: to model is to sit or pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A junior functionary is visible; then everyone sits back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MODEL into LEDOM. A beadle was a minor parish officer, so beadledom is that petty officialdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a lowly parish officer, and the suffix -dom gives the rank or realm of such petty officials.

clue.text: Left port with weighty cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship left harbour heavily loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened with goods.

clue.text: Dandies in back street cricket side

indicators.note: in puts the cricket side inside the reversed street
back says the abbreviation for street is written backwards

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, the side the batsman faces

explanation.surface: Smart young men playing cricket in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round to TS, and 'in' puts the cricket side between its letters. A cricket field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs are well-dressed upper-class people, the British equivalent of fashionable swells.

clue.text: In Asia he advanced in a forward direction

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man made progress while travelling through Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it begins a place phrase, but it signals the run A HE AD inside 'Asia he advanced'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front or onward, moving forward.

clue.text: Animal subspecies circumventing new obstacle

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the subspecies word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a race is a breed or subspecies of animal

explanation.surface: A zoologist's note about a breed of animal getting round a fresh barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumventing' wraps the subspecies word around the letter for new, making RANCE, after the female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that holds you back, an impediment.

clue.text: Students' leader leaves Oxford, perhaps, to work on the land

indicators.note: leaves means the leading letter departs from the footwear word

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of laced shoe

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word students

explanation.surface: The head of the student body quits the university to farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford, perhaps' suggests the university, but it is a lace-up shoe; 'leader' gives S, which 'leaves' takes away.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to break up soil and weed with a long-handled tool.

clue.text: Wine taken during current easing of tension

indicators.note: taken during means the wine is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a river is a current of water; the Dee is a British river
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, mostly used for communion

explanation.surface: Drinking wine while flowing water calms things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken during' puts the wine inside the river. Tent is an old name for a Spanish red; the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the English-Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is a relaxing of strained relations between nations.

clue.text: Great, say, supporting this dog

parts.note: great said aloud is a fire grate, and a metal firedog stands in it holding the logs up

explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal stand holding logs in a fireplace, also called a firedog.
